title: Show the jobs the scheduler will run next

blocks.text: The batch scheduler's dashboard has a "next up" panel. Operators use it to decide whether to hold a job before it starts, and the panel has to show exactly the jobs the worker will take next, in the order it will take them. `JobQueue` already serves the worker through `next()`.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/JobQueue.java`: `upcoming(k)`, the `k` jobs due soonest, soonest first, or all of them when fewer are queued.
When you're done, the panel matches what the worker then does, and looking at the panel never changes what the worker gets. About four lines in total.

cases.says: with fewer jobs queued than asked for, upcoming lists each of them, and an empty queue gives an empty list
upcoming(k) lists the k jobs due soonest in due order, not in the queue's internal order
calling upcoming takes no job off the queue: the worker still gets every job, soonest first

origin.section: A PriorityQueue Is Ordered Only at Its Head

concepts: A PriorityQueue's iterator, toString and stream follow its heap array, so only peek and poll see the order, and ties come out in no particular order.
